text: Never add `from __future__ import annotations` to agent.py. It turns the custom actions' type hints into strings, browser-use then cannot see browser_session and refuses to register report_issue and open_page, and every persona fails before its agent runs. v0.1.0 shipped exactly this and reported zero sessions; v0.1.1 fixed it. Linters and "modernise" passes add the import automatically: check the diff.

mcp_server.py must not use `from __future__ import annotations` either: the MCP SDK builds each tool's input schema from the function's real annotations. Same failure class as agent.py, different library.

walk() once dropped any persona whose task raised before its agent ran, so a broken setup (the v0.1.0 annotation bug) produced a run with no sessions that looked clean. A task exception must stay a crashed session row, and the all-crashed note must stay. Keep that when refactoring walk or adding new per-persona setup steps.

The guard self-test's foreign-frame probe must use a host that is not an app host. A GET to an app host is a permitted read, so it would pass the guard, the self-test would see no 403 and refuse to start every run. probes() skips app hosts among example.org, example.net and iana.org; an app that lists all three would hit StopIteration. Any new probe needs the same care.

The package needs Python 3.12 or newer: it nests same-quote f-strings (PEP 701), a SyntaxError at import on 3.11 and older. Every installer pins `--python 3.12` (action.yml, buildspec, test.sh). A stock macOS python3 is 3.9, which is why .brain/bin stays 3.9-compatible while the package does not.

Agent file-writing tools decode backslash-u escapes in the text they write, so a test or doc that needs the literal six characters (the guard's escaped-key cases in test_policy.py, the README's escaped publish_at example) silently gets the decoded character instead. Build such strings with chr(92) in code, and check the bytes on disk (grep -c, xxd) after writing.

Despite the QUIET flags, Chromium still sends about 50 requests per run to Google hosts (component updates, safe browsing, sign-in). The guard refuses them and the report folds them into one count of requests to other sites. They are not app findings and not a guard leak. Follow-up: plans/chromium-background-noise.md.

Never create a branch with the same name as a tag (for example a branch called v0.2.0). Then `git push origin v0.2.0` is ambiguous and some commands pick the tag, others the branch. Push tags by full ref: `git push origin refs/tags/vX.Y.Z`.

Finding fingerprints are a public contract: tickets hashes each one into the hidden marker of every GitHub issue it files, in users' repositories. Changing what goes into one (agent_fingerprint, the signal and journey fingerprints, checks.normalize, issue_key) changes every marker, and the next `tickets --github-issues` files every ticket again. 0.2.0 did this once, on purpose, with an upgrade note in the README Changes section. Any further change needs the same: a release note and a minor version bump.

The 8 gitignore tests in test_repo_hygiene.py (7 check-ignore cases plus the .env.example one) skip on CodeBuild, because deploy/aws/test.sh uploads a zip with no .git. A green CodeBuild run proves nothing about .gitignore; after touching it, also run `uv run --python 3.12 --extra dev pytest tests/test_repo_hygiene.py` locally.

test_no_file_names_other_products fails on any file in the tree, .brain included, that names certain other products (the FORBIDDEN pattern in test_repo_hygiene.py, split so grep does not find it). In this repo, call the consumer "the downstream app" and the project swarm-persona grew out of "an internal UX swarm".
